lexicalDispositions.decision: Centre practical teaching on Confucian thought/learning and its scholars. Select only 儒教 as necessary new support for sole ジュ. 儒学 can be a kana-supplied comparison, with substantial overlap rather than a strict religious/secular divide. 儒 itself has Confucianism/Confucianist/Chinese-scholar glosses; do not make every scholar or teacher a 儒. 儒仏 combines Confucianism and Buddhism, not evidence that they are identical. These noun/adjectival-noun families do not license an unrestricted Japanese adjective *儒な.

犬儒学派 is the philosophical Cynic school and 犬儒 is a cynic, not simply a Confucian school/person. Do not force the core Confucian gloss into every whole compound or present these as extra necessary support.

Scholar/teacher and evaluative scholar families retain their whole-word meanings. 師儒 is teacher/scholar, 俗儒 mediocre scholar, 腐儒 pedant/worthless scholar, 老儒 elderly Confucian scholar; 大儒 separately includes great Confucian scholar and a broader learned-person sense. No universal Confucian-only rule across all historical vocabulary.

朱儒/侏儒 and obsolete medical 侏儒症 are not useful core support or grounds for an invented dwarf meaning for ordinary 儒 compounds. 儒艮 is rare ateji for dugong, 儒良 is search-only ateji, and the sense is usually kana. ジュゴン has re_nokanji while じゅごん is separately present. Do not treat the katakana row as evidence for the written pair, silently remove flags, or split ateji into a claimed new character reading. No new animal/medical course or sensitive usage is needed.

Historical and combined-tradition families remain evidence, not mandatory new support. 藩儒 and 宋儒 carry historical flags; 焚書坑儒 is a historical idiom; 儒墨 is rare. Preserve local flags and both 漢儒 senses, including its Japanese Confucianist/sinologist glosses. Do not infer identity or geographical exclusivity from isolated kanji meanings.

comparisonDispositions.decision: 学ぶ supports studying a subject; 学問 and 思想 are broader academic-learning/thought nouns, not synonyms for the particular Confucian tradition. 教える includes tell/inform and preach as separate senses. Search-only 學ぶ/訓える and rare 学文/学門 remain local spelling flags. Practical example sentences may use study/learn without importing every secondary sense.

儒教 and 儒学 both have Confucianism glosses; the public sources qualify scholarly emphasis without a strict semantic partition. 宗教 is the wider religion/faith category, not another name for Confucianism, and 仏教 is Buddhism. 佛教 is outdated kanji usage. No new 仏教 article is required for 儒's only practice key.

儀式 means ceremony/rite/ritual, 僧侶 is Buddhist clergy, 優しい means kind/gentle. Together with the complete character records and actual 儀/僧/優 cards, these support proposed wrong meaning labels without treating related ritual/learning/religion topics as synonyms.
